stability: Anything not listed here — everything under _plan/ and _records/, and records.jsonl — is internal and may change without notice; integrating against those paths is unsupported. Raw model responses live at each bedrock-inference run's own prefix; window_manifest.json's inference_runs[] is the join.

shots.description: THE product: one validated metadata document per shot, JSONL in shot order — join to shots.json by shot_id for times

example.description: Ines steps out of a taxi onto a rain-slick city street and looks up at an office tower.
actions: Ines hauls a suitcase from the taxi

camera_motion.reveals: a dead gunman in the kitchen

shots.notes: One line per ANSWERED shot; unanswered shot_ids are listed in scenes.json's shots_gap, never fabricated here. The model never emits timestamps — shot times, timecodes and frame ranges live in the shot-segmentation run's shots.json, joined by shot_id. starts_new_scene is the REPAIRED flag (`false` wins on a flag/reason cross-pairing, both directions); boundary_reason is the model's answer VERBATIM even when the pairing was repaired — scenes.json's pairing_repairs[] lists every repair. All closed-vocabulary fields (shot_kind, camera_shot_type, setting, time_of_day, weather, lighting, notable, people_count, sentiment, carrier_type, evidence, confidence) use the prompt's exact terms. people[] carries ONLY face-recognition-supplied names. state_change is OPTIONAL and rare (~10% of shots, measured on the development corpus): present only when the shot's begin and end states differ materially — `what` (<=15 words, the change only) + `when` (early|mid|late within the shot); absent means no material change, never null. actions[] (cap 3, strings <=10 words, present tense) carries the physical business a one-sentence description drops — hands, objects, contact; expressions[] (cap 3, {who, shows<=6 words}) carries readable facial/bodily reaction and is populated only at framings tight enough to read a face; camera_motion is OPTIONAL like state_change ({kind: pan|tilt|push_in|pull_back|tracking|crane_rise|crane_descend|aerial_sweep, reveals<=10 words naming what the move discloses}, absent on static or single-frame shots). These three exist because measured professional AD (reference corpus, two drama series, 2026-08-28) spends most of its non-credit gap on exactly this material; [] / absent are the expected majority answers.

scenes.description: Scenes assembled deterministically from the repaired starts_new_scene flags, with code-aggregated attributes and per-scene shot descriptions
scenes.notes: Scene attributes are AGGREGATED IN CODE across member shots (majority vote for setting/time_of_day/sentiment, name-deduped unions for people/brands/named_entities) — never read off a single shot, because per-window independence measurably drifts attributes inside one scene. pairing_repair_rate is a usable interleaved-genre signal: ~0 on linear content (scripted drama, film), 2-8% on interleaved content (news, current affairs; measured on the development corpus) — where flags alone under-segment and a grouping pass over this file is the designed follow-up. Scene times come from shots.json, never from the model.

window-manifest.description: Traceability by POINTER: the window plan (shot_ids, context shot, image blocks, resolved flag) and the bedrock-inference run entries
window-manifest.notes: inference_runs[].output_s3_prefix is the bedrock run: request.jsonl there is the EXACT rendered bytes (the question), response.jsonl the raw model output per window (join by record_id window-NNN), summary.json the authoritative outcome and cost. Raw responses are never copied here — this file is the join.

usage.description: Aggregated spend across the run's bedrock-inference submissions, with the cost_is_complete discipline
usage.notes: Costs are estimates from bedrock-inference's own summaries; cost_is_complete=false means at least one run's summary lacked a figure. Each run's own usage_tracking.json (usage_uri) carries the per-state breakdown.
